title: Attributes
description: Classify ER attributes by meaning, structure, multiplicity and derivation, then map descriptive roles to consistent SQL projections and relationship facts.
notes:
## Attributes describe entities and relationships

An attribute records a property of an entity or relationship in an entity-relationship model. Student can have a student identifier, display name, and date of birth. An Enrollment relationship can have a grade and enrollment date. The attribute belongs with the occurrence whose property it describes, rather than whichever table has a convenient empty column in the implementation.

For example, a grade for one student's attempt at one course does not describe that student's single permanent universal grade. It describes the relevant enrollment or assessment occurrence. If the student takes three courses, three separate grades can belong to three related facts. Correct ownership of attributes begins with the meaning of one occurrence and the identifying relationships in the model.

## Distinguish the name from its value

The attribute name supplies a role shared by the modeled type. Its value describes one particular occurrence. Student_name is the role, while Asha is a value in one student's record. Another student can have a different value, and two different students can share Asha without becoming one entity. Repeated descriptions must not silently replace the intended identifying rule.

An attribute is also different from the entire entity set. Date_of_birth is a property, not the collection of all students. A relationship such as Enrollment connects identified participants, while enrollment_date describes that participation. A model that confuses these roles can store an attribute at the wrong grain and make later updates overwrite information about unrelated occurrences.

## Domains describe permitted values

A domain supplies the values permitted for an attribute's meaning. A grade-point average might use a documented bounded decimal scale, while a date of birth uses the relevant date representation and validity policy. The attribute label alone does not prove the exact grade scale or every acceptable date. Those details belong in the requirements and chosen enforcement contract.

An SQL type is part of the implementation, but it may not encode the whole domain. A numeric type can represent negative credits even if the institutional policy forbids them. Required-value and range constraints express different ingredients. Similarly, a string width limits representation without proving that a supplied programme code belongs to the actual catalogue. Match the implementation to the complete intended property.

## Structure and multiplicity are independent

A simple attribute is treated as one value without separately modeled components for the application's purposes. A composite attribute has useful subcomponents, such as a contact address with street, city, and postal code. This structural distinction does not decide how many such values can belong to one entity. One structured address can be both composite and single-valued.

A student can instead have several structured addresses, making the property composite and multivalued. A telephone number can be treated as one simple domain value while several telephone values belong to one student. Keep these dimensions separate. Neither a long string nor several component fields by itself establishes that the entity has several independent occurrences of the property.

## Stored and derived describe another dimension

A stored attribute records an input fact, such as a date of birth or an assessment score. A derived attribute is calculated under a stated rule from other facts, such as a total credit count at a defined time. A property can be simple and derived, or composite and stored. These classifications answer different questions about representation and origin.

Derived values need a calculation contract. Age depends on the reference date and calendar interpretation, so it is not a timeless number obtained by subtracting years without considering birthdays. A course total depends on which registrations qualify. Do not treat a derived label as a guarantee that any convenient arithmetic expression computes the intended quantity. State its source population, units, and reference point.

## Missing information does not remove the role

An optional phone attribute can be absent for a student while remaining part of the type's definition. In a nullable SQL mapping, NULL can represent the documented absence. That does not shorten the row or erase the attribute from every other student. A required attribute has a different policy and should reject an unsupported missing value through the appropriate boundary.

A blank string, zero, and the literal text NULL are ordinary values with meanings different from SQL absence. Replacing every missing property with one placeholder can lose distinctions or distort aggregates. Explain whether absence means unknown, not yet supplied, or inapplicable. If those causes require different actions, an explicit reason or status may be needed rather than expecting one NULL marker to encode them all.

## Notation communicates the chosen distinctions

In common Chen-style diagrams, attributes are shown using ovals attached to the relevant entity or relationship. A key uses the convention's identifying mark, a multivalued attribute has a double oval, and a derived attribute can use a dashed oval. A composite property connects to component attributes. Other notations may draw these same concepts differently.

A drawing does not itself enforce SQL types, uniqueness, or nullability. It communicates the logical design and its assumptions. Verify the actual mapping and supported constraints separately. Avoid interpreting a diagram symbol as evidence that every input is validated or that every user has permission to view the described property. Descriptive modeling and trusted access remain different concerns.

## Map simple roles explicitly

A straightforward relational mapping can place a simple single-valued property in a column alongside the entity identifier. Use an explicit SQL projection when a report needs only selected roles. An alias can label the output without changing a stored attribute name. This keeps an application result contract stable when unrelated source properties are added later.

```sql
SELECT student_id, student_name AS display_name
FROM students
WHERE contact_email IS NULL
ORDER BY student_id;
```

The query identifies students whose optional contact email is absent under the supplied policy. It does not return a distinct set of names; two students named Asha remain two identified facts. The display_name alias belongs to the result and does not rename the persistent column or alter any student's name.

## Relationship attributes need participant identities

Suppose Enrollment stores enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, and score. The score belongs to the enrollment occurrence. A report joining Student to Enrollment can include student_name and course-specific score, but it should retain the relevant identifiers so separate participations stay distinguishable. A student with two enrollments can correctly appear twice in this relationship-grain result.

A missing score and a recorded zero are different states. A condition asking for recorded scores should use the appropriate presence predicate rather than a truthy numeric shortcut that excludes zero. An unrecorded grade should not be silently converted to a failing grade unless the business rule explicitly defines that treatment. Attribute meaning controls correct filtering and calculation.

## More complex properties need suitable mappings

A multivalued contact property commonly maps to a separate relation containing the owner identity and one row per value. A composite property can map to component columns, with another relation when multiplicity or independent lifecycle requires it. A shared catalogue such as Programme may be better represented as an entity with a relationship rather than repeatedly copying its descriptive details into student records.

These are mapping choices guided by the actual facts. They are not universal instructions to create a new entity for every label or a separate table for every character inside a string. Ask which components and occurrences need independent queries, validity rules, and updates. The smallest coherent representation should preserve that meaning without arbitrary parallel copies.

## Review an attribute definition as a contract

For each property, state its owner occurrence, domain, optionality, structural components, multiplicity, and any derivation rule. Identify the roles that supply identity and those that only describe it. Use repeated names, absent contact details, recorded zero scores, and several relationship occurrences as counterexamples when reviewing queries. A fixture containing only unique complete values can hide many modeling mistakes.

The exercises demonstrate selected relational mappings and result contracts on isolated SQL data. They do not establish every ER transformation, external fact, or production permission. Clear attribute modeling connects the meaning of a property to the correct occurrence and implementation boundary. That makes later discussions of simple, composite, single-valued, multivalued, stored, and derived attributes consistent rather than a disconnected list of diagram shapes.

questions.question_text: What is an attribute in the ER model?
options: A relationship between two entity sets
A property or characteristic that describes an entity (or relationship)
A rectangle in an ER diagram
A synonym for entity set
questions.explanation: Attributes are the descriptive details attached to entities (and relationships), such as Name or CGPA for a Student.

questions.question_text: In the stated model where Course and Department are entity types and Enrollment is a relationship, which choice is a descriptive Student attribute?
options: Enrollment
Course
Date_of_Birth
Department
questions.explanation: Date_of_Birth is a descriptive property of a Student entity, unlike Course/Department/Enrollment which are separate entities/relationships.

questions.question_text: What is the 'domain' of an attribute?
options: The physical table it is stored in
The set of legal/permitted values the attribute may take
Another name for the primary key
The entity set it belongs to
questions.explanation: The domain defines the valid range or set of values, e.g., CGPA between 0.0 and 10.0.

questions.question_text: Can attributes be attached to a relationship, not just to an entity?
options: No, only entities can have attributes
Yes — e.g., Grade and Enrollment_Date logically describe the Enrollment relationship between Student and Course
Only weak entities' relationships can have attributes
Only recursive relationships can have attributes
questions.explanation: Relationships can carry their own descriptive attributes, distinct from the attributes of the entities they connect.

questions.question_text: When the model permits an absent optional phone and maps it to a nullable SQL column, how can unknown phone information be represented?
options: The attribute is deleted from the entity set
As NULL for that entity's value of that attribute
As the value zero
The entity is deleted
questions.explanation: A permitted NULL represents the defined absence; it does not erase the attribute role. Required inputs have a separate policy.

questions.question_text: Which of these is the correct general relationship between 'Attributes' and its subtypes (simple, composite, derived, etc.)?
options: They are unrelated concepts
'Attributes' is the umbrella category; simple/composite, single/multi-valued, and stored/derived are classification dimensions within it
Only composite attributes are real attributes; the rest are a misnomer
Derived attributes are not attributes at all
questions.explanation: All these subtypes classify different characteristics of the general concept 'attribute'.

questions.question_text: Why can two entities of the same entity set have different attribute values?
options: Because each entity is a distinct occurrence, and attributes hold instance-specific values drawn from the same defined set of attributes
Because entity sets allow different attribute names per entity
Because attributes are randomly regenerated
This is not possible; all entities of a set must share identical values
questions.explanation: The entity set defines which attributes exist; each entity instance supplies its own value for each.

questions.question_text: Which statement is FALSE about attributes?
options: Every attribute value must fall within the attribute's defined domain
Attributes can only exist on strong entities, never on weak entities or relationships
An attribute may be NULL if the value is unknown
Attributes describe properties of entities or relationships
questions.explanation: Weak entities and relationships can also have attributes — this restriction is false.

questions.question_text: Where does the grade for one student-course attempt belong?
options: As one universal student grade for every course
With that assessment or enrollment occurrence
As the course title
As the programme identifier
questions.explanation: Property ownership follows the fact grain.

questions.question_text: Can one structured address be both composite and single-valued?
options: No; composite always means many addresses
Only if absent
Yes; structure and multiplicity are separate dimensions
Only if every component is numeric
questions.explanation: One value can contain several meaningful components.

questions.question_text: Does a simple phone value imply each student may have only one phone?
options: Yes; simple implies one occurrence
Only if the number is short
No; simplicity and multiplicity differ
Only if the number is a key
questions.explanation: Several simple values can form a multivalued property.

questions.question_text: What does a result alias such as student_name AS display_name change?
options: The stored name value
Every source attribute
The identifying policy
The output label
questions.explanation: Projection labels do not perform persistent schema changes.

questions.question_text: Why keep student_id when listing missing contact details?
options: Different students can share descriptive names
A name is always unique
NULL removes the identifier automatically
A display label grants access
questions.explanation: Identifiers preserve the intended entity occurrences.

questions.question_text: What makes a derived age calculation meaningful?
options: Only subtracting two year numbers universally
A defined reference date and calendar rule
A short alias
A specific font
questions.explanation: Age needs a precise derivation contract.

questions.question_text: Does VARCHAR width establish that a programme code belongs to the catalogue?
options: Yes; all strings in range are valid programmes
Only if sorted
No; representation and catalogue validity differ
Only if the table is empty
questions.explanation: Additional relationship or membership enforcement may be needed.

questions.question_text: How should recorded zero scores be treated in a recorded-score listing?
options: Always exclude them as absent
Replace them with NULL
Treat them as a separate entity type
As recorded values, distinct from missing scores
questions.explanation: Presence is not the same as a nonzero numeric value.

questions.question_text: Can a relationship have its own descriptive date?
options: Yes; the date can describe that participation occurrence
No; dates only belong to entities
Only weak types can have dates
Only a primary key can store dates
questions.explanation: Relationship attributes follow the participation facts.

questions.question_text: Does a diagram oval execute input validation?
options: Yes; every oval creates a CHECK
No; it communicates the model
Only if double-lined
Only if the label is numeric
questions.explanation: Implementation and evidence remain separate.

questions.question_text: Why might Programme be an entity rather than copied text?
options: Every short string must be an entity
All descriptive attributes require new tables
It can have an independent catalogue identity, properties and relationships
Text cannot be stored in a relation
questions.explanation: The lifecycle and relationships can justify a separate entity.

questions.question_text: Which questions form a useful attribute review?
options: Only colour and position
Only current sample length
Only the attribute’s alphabetic order
Owner occurrence, domain, optionality, structure, multiplicity and derivation
questions.explanation: These dimensions define the property contract.

coding_problems.title: Project identified students with missing contact information
coding_problems.task: Return student_id and student_name AS display_name where contact_email is SQL NULL. Preserve different student identities sharing a name.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, contact_email VARCHAR(80) NULL);
constraints: Absence is represented by NULL; an empty string is a separate stored value.
edge_cases: A blank-looking empty string is not NULL.
hints: Use IS NULL for the documented absence.
The alias affects the output label only.
coding_problems.solution_sql: SELECT student_id, student_name AS display_name FROM students WHERE contact_email IS NULL ORDER BY student_id;
coding_problems.explanation: The projection preserves entity identity while displaying only requested attribute roles.

coding_problems.title: Keep scores attached to their enrollment occurrences
coding_problems.task: Return enrollment_id, student_id, student_name, course_id and score for enrollments with a recorded score. Include zero scores and preserve separate enrollment occurrences.
coding_problems.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE enrollments (enrollment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT NOT NULL, course_id INT NOT NULL, score INT NULL);
coding_problems.seed_sql: INSERT INTO students VALUES (1,'Asha'),(2,'Asha'); INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (1,1,10,0),(2,1,20,90),(3,2,10,NULL);
coding_problems.expected:
enrollment_id	student_id	student_name	course_id	score
1	1	Asha	10	0
2	1	Asha	20	90
constraints: All supplied enrollment student references match students; native FK enforcement is outside these temporary mirrors.
edge_cases: One student can have multiple enrollment-specific scores.
Zero and missing scores are distinct.
hints: Select the participation identity and use IS NOT NULL for recorded scores.
coding_problems.solution_sql: SELECT e.enrollment_id, s.student_id, s.student_name, e.course_id, e.score FROM enrollments e JOIN students s ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.score IS NOT NULL ORDER BY e.enrollment_id;
coding_problems.explanation: The score remains associated with the specific participation rather than becoming one universal student property.

validation_cases.seed_sql: INSERT INTO students VALUES (7,'Mira'); INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (2,7,10,0),(1,7,10,80);
validation_cases.expected:
enrollment_id	student_id	student_name	course_id	score
1	7	Mira	10	80
2	7	Mira	10	0
